craft_notes: Sthāyin: seal — the whole Heart in one name. Sanskrit-first: bhava (BECOME — imperative kept); śivaḥ (ŚIVA — single-word close; the name IS the period). Abhinavagupta frame: becoming ends IN the name (no predicate beyond it — the verse refuses to say more, and the refusal IS the seal). Rows: 6 (Śiva as seal-word, verbatim, never reworded), 1 (‘Śiva’ closes — becoming lands IN the name), 12 (whole-WORK śānta-fall into the name). Close: ‘Śiva’. Rupture: em-dash (command, then the name — everything funnels). Rejected: anything more — killed: Śiva is the period; ‘become Śiva!’ exclamation — killed: stillness kept (comma-period, not shout). Read aloud: be-COME, then — … ŚI-va.

reads_against.argmap: What seals the Heart? → Close in becoming: opening, means, recall, Śiva.
c1_essence: Opening middle, given means, recalled oneness, become Śiva.
